name: NEON WASP
purpose: Original-style 3D modeling concept handoff; not a finished 3D mesh or engineering drawing
scale_status: All dimensions and colors are suggested art-direction targets, not measurements extracted from the generated image.

coordinates.origin: Ground plane, midway between front and rear axles, on vehicle centerline
coordinates.front_steering_axis: Z approximation; artist may add kingpin inclination

construction_notes: Silhouette priority: a narrow pointed yellow nose, lots of open space between the chassis and wheels, purple cage, and TWO separated yellow rear fins.
Keep the nose, side panels and fins as thin shells with finished undersides; do not fill the open chassis into a solid body.
Use a central rear motor/battery enclosure low behind the seat. Mount two compact boosters above it, parallel to the forward axis, with their nozzles facing backward.
Rear fin attachments and underside structure are new proposed details. Keep the fins paired and mirrored; do not reinterpret them as one central spoiler.
Use cyan rim bands and suspension springs, violet tube frame and yellow panel masses. Purple fin stripes are decals.
The image views are approximate: match front and rear axle positions to the written wheelbase; normalize fin height, booster spacing and cage width in the first blockout.
source_precedence: Original concept sheet for character, silhouette, colors and visible styling
This written specification for proposed dimensions and explicit consistency resolutions
Turnaround sheet for supplemental shape guidance; new hidden surfaces are design proposals

material_starting_points.emissive: Separate mask; tune intensity in the target engine. Palette hex values are sRGB, not linear shader values.

rig_notes: Root at the specified origin; bind chassis to vehicle body control.
Wheel pivots at axle centers. Keep tire and rim aligned; steering upright parents wheel spin on front corners.
Pivot suspension arms at inboard attachment points; use look-at/constraints or baked animation for shocks.
Keep steering wheel, springs, fan rotors and emissive boost meshes separate as applicable.
Leave fenders and cage on the chassis; test wheel clearance at full steering, bump and droop.
Export axes depend on the target engine; the coordinate convention here is the modeling master convention.
